subject: Endpoint cost heatmap + deprioritization playbook request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kate Long <kate@acme.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Endpoint cost heatmap + deprioritization playbook request

Hey team,

Quick ask from the Acme renewal/expansion thread — they want a way in Console to instantly surface which "micro-endpoints" (per-route / per-tool call slices) are driving token spend and tail latency over time. The ask has two parts: a) a heatmap + timeline view that lets us pivot by route, model variant, and tenant; and b) a documented playbook + automated signal (deprioritization/fallback) so product teams can safely reduce spend during capacity or budget pressure.

Acme shared an internal use-case: during big batch jobs they see a handful of low-value routes that balloon token spend and push up p99. They want to:
- see a 7/30/90-day heatmap to spot recurring offenders
- click into a route to see cost trend, token distribution, and top callers (tenant IDs or labels)
- configure an action (soft deprioritize, route to cheaper model variant, or enable local caching) with clear expected cost reduction and latency impact.

I've attached a quick mockup (heatmap-mockup-v2.png) and a short MVP gap list (mvp-gap-list.xlsx). Can you confirm feasibility and provide an ETA (MVP vs full)? Specific questions:
1) What instrumentation changes do we need server-side to attribute cost per micro-route with acceptable overhead?
2) Can we realistically support tenant-level pivots in the UI without exploding query cost for Console analytics?
3) For the deprioritization action, what primitives exist today (routing policy, model variants, rate-limits) and what needs to be built?

Kate — feel free to add any customer nuance. I promised Acme I'd give an internal feasibility and a timeline this week so they can plan for Q4 renewals.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor

On Tue, Sep 14, 2027 at 9:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick ask from the Acme renewal/expansion thread — they want a way in Console to instantly surface which "micro-endpoints" are driving token spend and tail latency over time.

Thanks Neha — this is great context and the mockup helps. A couple quick clarifying items from the product/observability side before we scope: 

- Granularity: do we need per-API-route + per-caller-id (tenant) for the MVP, or is per-route aggregated across tenants acceptable initially?
- SLOs: what are the critical SLOs here (p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens)? That will drive both the UX and how we surface deviations/alerts.
- Signal latency: are 5–15 minute resolution windows okay, or does Acme need near-real-time (sub-1min)?

I'll pull in Ops/Infra if we need changes to runtime tagging. Markus — any immediate concerns on storage/query cost or existing metrics we can reuse?

Monica
Director, Observability Product
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kate Long <kate@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Endpoint cost heatmap + deprioritization playbook request

Monica — good questions. High-level assessment:

- Instrumentation: we currently emit per-request metadata (route, model, tenant hash, token counts) but not always indexed in a way that supports fast ad-hoc pivots. We can add a compact attribution index that stores (route, tenant_label, model_variant, tokens, timestamp) with weekly rollups. Cost: extra storage + ingestion CPU; estimate ~8–12% extra infra for heavy customers.

- Query/aggregation approach: MVP should use pre-aggregated rollups (1m/5m windows) and an on-demand drill path that queries raw logs for deep dives. That keeps Console query cost bounded while giving drillability.

- Deprioritization primitives: we already have routing policies and model-variant fallbacks, plus a soft-rate-limit hook used by Dedicated. Missing pieces: a UI flow to tie a heatmap cell -> create routing rule + dry-run metrics; and a simulation pane that shows expected cost delta (estimated tokens saved) before applying.

Phased proposal (short):
1) MVP (8–10w): heatmap + timeline with 1m/5m rollups, tenant pivot (hashed IDs), drill-to-raw link; simple "suggested action" CTA (manual runbook entry).
2) Phase 2 (12–18w): UI action to create a deprioritization rule (soft limit, model fallback), simulation engine, and audit trail.
3) Phase 3 (quarter+): automated policy engine that can run rules during capacity events (requires infra safeguards + customer opt-in).

I'll attach an MVP gap list (see mvp-gap-list.xlsx) with infra tickets and expected owners. We should also flag an SLA exception pattern: if a tenant is deprioritized, we need explicit consent and an audit event.

-Markus
VP, Serving Platform
markus.klein@redwood.com

Thanks Monica/Markus — this is exactly what Acme needs to push the conversation forward.

Next steps I propose:
- Markus: please paste the MVP ticket IDs and estimated owners into OPS-1324 this week (I linked it above).
- Monica: can you draft the UI acceptance criteria for the heatmap (granularity, pivot controls, drill UX) so I can share with Acme by EOD Friday?
- Neha (me): I'll confirm with Acme that hashed tenant-level pivots are acceptable and get back with any carve-outs.

Kate — if you can confirm the business priority (Q4 pilot vs Q1 roadmapped), we can prioritize accordingly on our side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. If we keep to the proposed 8–10w MVP we should have something demonstrable before Acme's renewal.

Best,
